annotationRationale: The decisive step expands the sine of a sum and bounds its terms using inequality properties. Sine signs and the cosine upper bound justify those comparisons.
sourceMethod: Follows the official sine-addition proof, spelling out the two termwise inequalities.

review.mathCheck: For every x,y in [0,π], both sine factors are nonnegative and both cosines are at most 1. Multiplying and adding therefore bounds sin(x+y) by sin x+sin y, including endpoints. Every allowed y works, so E is the largest subset.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 9 on page 3. It uses the same addition-formula bound and makes the two termwise comparisons explicit.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed identity and inequality properties, supported by trigonometric signs and the cosine bound, match the argument. No alternative method or additional node is needed.
